premises.text: Current illness detection happens after symptoms via slow manual PCR community testing
premises.evidence_span: We are then doing it manually by doing PCR tests

premises.text: Sewage surveillance detects one sick person in 10,000 and works for symptomatic and asymptomatic infection
premises.evidence_span: you can detect one sick person in 10,000 people

premises.text: Manual sewer-to-lab workflows take up to a week and cost up to $1,000, arriving too late
premises.evidence_span: when an organization like the CDC gets their data, it's already too late and outbreaks already happened

premises.text: Automated multi-stage hardware keeps the dirtiest filtrate, extracts RNA, and runs continuous collective qPCR
premises.evidence_span: We're keeping the dirtiest sample. We filter hundreds of liters of water each and every day

premises.text: Installable building systems detect multiple pathogens and push same-day dashboard risk insights to customers

premises.text: Workplaces and nursing homes can act before symptoms (e.g., norovirus two days early)
